title: Amazon Is Gutting Its AI Division After Sustained Failure
content:
By now, you’d be hard pressed to find anyone who isn’t broadly familiar with the AI heavyweights and their flagship models. OpenAI has ChatGPT, Anthropic has Claude, Google has Gemini. But what does Amazon have?
Not a whole lot, it turns out. Unlike its competitors in the tech megacorp scene, Amazon’s standout AI model — organized under the name “Nova” — is about the farthest thing from a household name. And that’s not likely to change anytime soon, because the ecommerce giant is now gutting its in-house AI labs, Bloomberg reports.
Per the outlet, Amazon is scaling back the ambitions of most of its Nova AI models and reorganizing its AI development teams as part of an effort to narrow its focus on “highest priority” goals, after its power-hungry large language models turned out to be a bust.
Accordingly, the company has put most of its AI models on ice, Amazon insiders told Bloomberg. This includes its text-based Nova models, as well as video- and image-generating models, all of which have been placed in a state of “keep the lights on,” meaning they’re technically still supported, but only receive the bare minimum resources needed to sustain them.
Instead, labor and computing power are being diverted toward a singular “frontier-model effort” led by Pieter Abbeel, director of the Berkeley Robot Learning Lab whose robotics company Covariant was hoovered up by Amazon in 2024. At the time Abbeel joined the tech giant, Covariant’s founders were working on AI models for robots, which lines up pretty well with Amazon’s push to automate everything it possibly can.
News of the shift in Amazon’s strategic focus comes a week after it closed one of its key AI offices in San Francisco, an 80-person site specializing in research on artificial general intelligence, the supposed next-level of AI development where the tech obtains human-level intelligence and reasoning skills.
With urgent questions swirling over whether LLMs can ever usher in a return on investment — let alone AGI — it may be that Amazon is jumping out of the AI hype cycle while it still can.

report.summary: Amazon is scaling back its Nova AI models and reorganizing teams to focus on a single frontier-model effort after struggling to compete in the LLM race.
report.background: Amazon is one of the world’s largest cloud and technology companies, but it has not produced a flagship large language model with the consumer recognition of OpenAI’s ChatGPT, Anthropic’s Claude, or Google’s Gemini. Its Nova family of models was intended to change that, spanning text, image, and video generation. Yet Nova remained far from a household name, and Bloomberg reports that Amazon is now narrowing its AI ambitions after power-hungry LLMs failed to deliver expected results. The reorg comes amid broader industry scrutiny over whether massive LLM investments can produce returns—or lead to AGI. Amazon had also recently closed an 80-person San Francisco office focused on AGI research, signaling a retreat from broad, long-horizon AI research toward more targeted priorities.
key_points: Amazon has placed most Nova models—including text, image, and video generators—into “keep the lights on” mode, meaning they remain technically supported but receive only bare-minimum resources while staff and compute are redirected elsewhere.

The company is consolidating around a single “frontier-model effort” led by Pieter Abbeel, director of the Berkeley Robot Learning Lab, whose robotics startup Covariant Amazon acquired in 2024. The focus aligns with Amazon’s broader automation and robotics push.
Amazon closed an 80-person San Francisco office dedicated to AGI research just a week before the reorganization, reinforcing that it is stepping back from ambitious, open-ended AI research bets.
The shift reflects growing doubts about LLM return on investment and Amazon’s inability to turn Nova into a major competitor against ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini despite its cloud scale and resources.
report.impact: For the AI industry, Amazon’s pullback is a signal that the frontier-model race is becoming a capital-intensive contest dominated by a few players, and that even megacorps can retrench when returns are unclear. For developers, the message is to avoid assuming Nova will be a long-term default: multi-model platforms like Bedrock and portable, open-weight alternatives become safer bets. Enterprise customers may hedge across providers rather than standardize on Amazon’s in-house models. For regular users, the effect is likely fewer visible Amazon-branded AI products and features, even as Amazon quietly redirects AI talent toward robotics, automation, and cloud services where it sees clearer commercial advantage.
report.tools: Watch Amazon Bedrock for multi-model access, SageMaker for enterprise ML workflows, and any remaining Nova frontier model. For alternatives, explore Hugging Face, Meta’s Llama, Mistral, vLLM, and Ollama for open-weight experimentation. Covariant and Abbeel’s robotics work are also worth following as indicators of Amazon’s applied-AI direction.
